title: Pan Grilled Pork Chops
description:
We really like pork chops, but getting them to cook right is a difficult task. Thanks to genetic manipulation, today’s pork has about 30 percent less fat than it did just a few decades ago, and less fat means blander, drier meat. But, because the once-feared trichinosis in pork has been all but totally eliminated (at least in the U.S.), pork doesn’t have to be cooked until it has the chewiness of leather.
This technique from Cook’s Illustrated does the trick of producing a juicy interior and a caramelized exterior.
START TO FINISH: 1 HOUR + 45 MIN
IF TIME PERMITS
Pan-Grilled Pork Chops
Preheat oven to 275 degrees.
Pat chops dry with paper towels. Using sharp knife, cut 2 slits, about 2 inches apart, through outer layer of fat and silver skin.
Sprinkle entire surface of each chop with 1 teaspoon salt. Place chops on wire rack set in rimmed baking sheet and let stand at room temperature 45 minutes (if time permits).
Season chops liberally with pepper; transfer baking sheet to oven. Cook around 30 minutes (or less if your chops are not 1 ½ inches thick), or until instant-read thermometer inserted into centers of chops and away from bones registers about 120 degrees.
ingredients: 4 pork loin chops, preferably with the bone in,
1 ½ inches thick, about 12 ounces each
3 tablespoons cold unsalted butter, cut into 3 pieces
directions: For the sauce, pour off all but 1 teaspoon oil from pan used to cook chops and return pan to medium heat.
Add shallot and garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until softened, about 1 minute.
Add wine and broth, scraping pan bottom to loosen browned bits.
Simmer until reduced to 1/2 cup, 6 to 7 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in thyme and vinegar, then whisk in butter, 1 tablespoon at a time. Season with salt and pepper and serve with chops.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in 12-inch heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat until smoking. Place chops in a skillet and sear until well browned and crusty, 1 to 2 minutes, lifting once halfway through to redistribute fat underneath each chop. (Reduce heat if browned bits in pan bottom start to burn.) Using tongs, turn chops and cook until well browned on second side, another 1 to 2 minutes.
Transfer chops to plate let them rest, loosely tented with foil, for 10 minutes while preparing sauce.
